sentences.text: This small marine reptile measured approximately 79.4 centimeters in length and likely consumed soft-bodied prey.
Thickened ribs and a small pelvis suggest it rarely left the water.
The genus was first identified at the Sonshugo locality in Hubei, China.
A more complete specimen was described in 2022 from the Yingzishan locality in Hubei.
Scientists believe its long trunk and tiny limbs allowed it to swim using its body axis.
Originally thought to be a thalattosaur, later research placed it within Sauropterygia.
Its placement within Sauropterygia has varied across different scientific studies.
A 2024 study positioned it as the sister taxon to Nothosauroidea and Pachypleurosauria.
The Paleobi Database currently lists its parent group as Pachypleurosauridae.
Fossils were found in a formation interpreted as a lagoon deposit near the sea.
Some researchers argue that differences in coracoid shape suggest the more complete specimen might belong to a different species, Lariosaurus, rather than Hanosaurus.
